title: Sources of income and wealth
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers where people's income comes from or how wealth is measured as assets less debts, so this needs a new point; national income (e-income) and consumption (e-consumption) are related but cover different ideas.

draft.title: Sources of income and wealth
card: Income is a flow of money received over a period of time, such as a year. It comes from wages and salaries, profits, interest, rent and welfare payments.
Wealth is a stock measured at one point in time. It is the value of assets, less debts. Assets include housing, shares and superannuation.
Each source of income links to an asset or an activity. Wages come from work, profits from owning a business, interest from money lent, and rent from property let to others.
Welfare payments are income from the government. A person can have a high income and little wealth, or the reverse, such as a retiree who owns a home but earns little.
draft.remember: Income is what you receive over a period. Wealth is what you own, less what you owe, at one time.

a.q: Which of these is part of a household's wealth, not its income?
opts: The value of its home, less the home loan
The wages earned by its members this year
The rent received from a flat it lets out
The interest paid on its savings account
a.why: Wealth is the value of assets less debts, measured at one point in time. The home is an asset and the loan is a debt. Rent received is tempting, but it is a flow of money over time, so it is income.
a.clue: Wealth is a stock at one time, not a flow over a year.

b.q: Priya is a retired teacher in Ballarat. She owns her home outright, and her only money each year is a small part-pension. How is her position best described?
opts: Considerable wealth but a low income
Considerable wealth and a high income
Little wealth but a high income
Little wealth and a low income
b.why: Her home is a large asset with no debt, so her wealth is considerable. Her yearly money received is small, so her income is low. The tempting answer is low wealth, but a small income does not mean small wealth.
b.clue: Compare what she owns with what she receives each year.

a.best: The value of its home, less the home loan

b.best: Considerable wealth but a low income
